## Synthesis: research report

**Question:** Research Shiprocket (Indian logistics/ecommerce-enablement company, CEO Saahil Goel) as a prospective employer for an early-career AI/full-stack engineer deciding between a Shiprocket AI-team offer and an existing 22 LPA offer from BNY (Bank of New York Mellon) India. Cover, with sources and dates:

1. Work culture & employee sentiment: Glassdoor/AmbitionBox/Blind/Reddit reviews — overall ratings, work-life balance, management quality, toxicity complaints, attrition, layoffs/restructuring history, PIP culture, hiring/firing patterns. Distinguish engineering reviews from ops/sales reviews where possible.
2. Company health: funding history, valuation, profitability/financials (FY24/FY25 results), IPO plans/status as of mid-2026, major business risks (e.g., dependence on D2C/Shopify sellers, competition from Delhivery/Pickrr/Shipway etc.), any recent controversies or news.
3. Compensation benchmarks: what Shiprocket pays software/AI engineers (AmbitionBox/Levels.fyi/6figr data), typical SDE-1/SDE-2 bands, ESOP practices, and how a ~22 LPA offer compares; also typical BNY Mellon India comp/culture for contrast.
4. Leadership: reputation of CEO Saahil Goel; anything public about Parikshit Joon and Tanish Girotra (LinkedIn presence, background, prior work). The candidate would join a small 3-4 person 'startup inside a startup' AI team reporting to the CEO building agentic commerce / AI agents for sellers (memory+context layer, possibly a custom Chromium browser).
5. Shiprocket's AI strategy: public announcements about AI agents, agentic commerce, MCP servers, Saahil Goel's public statements/podcasts/posts on AI-native plans — to gauge whether this is a funded strategic priority or a CEO passion project that could be deprioritized.
6. Risk assessment factors: what happens to such teams historically, signals of stability (does Shiprocket have history of killing experimental projects, acqui-hires like Pickrr/Omuni/Wigzo and their outcomes).

Deliver a balanced report with citations, clearly flagging unverified/low-confidence claims, and end with a practical decision framework comparing the Shiprocket AI role vs the BNY 22 LPA offer for a young engineer (career growth, learning, comp, stability, brand value).

14 claims survived 3-vote adversarial verification. Merge semantic duplicates and synthesize.

## Confirmed claims
### [0] Shiprocket launched what it claims is India's first Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for eCommerce shipping in May 2025, demonstrating that agentic-commerce/AI infrastructure was already a shipped product (not just rhetoric) at least a year before mid-2026. The 'India's first' superlative is company-asserted and unverified independently.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://cxotoday.com/press-release/shiprocket-launches-indias-first-ai-integrated-mcp-server-for-ecommerce/ (primary)
Quote: "Shiprocket, India's leading eCommerce enablement platform, has launched the country's first Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server for eCommerce Shipping. This breakthrough innovation allows AI agents to directly handle key operations—from checking shipping rates to tracking orders—using a single line of instruction."
Verifier evidence (high): Claim verified on all counts. (1) Date: PTI wire brief carried by The Week on 2025-05-17 (theweek.in/wire-updates/business/2025/05/17/dcm30-biz-brief.html, auto-generated from PTI) reports Shiprocket unveiling what it describes as India's first AI-integrated MCP server for eCommerce shipping; the same release ran on Maritime Gateway and CXOToday (the cited primary, under /press-release/). (2) 'Shipped product, not rhetoric': independently confirmed by the actual artifact — github.com/bfrs/shiprocket-mcp under the bfrs org (Bigfoot Retail Solutions, Shiprocket's parent entity), GitHub API created_at 2025-05-05, pushed_at 2026-03-25 (actively maintained), 27 stars, exposing real tools (shipping_rate_calculator, estimated_date_of_delivery, order create/cancel/track, pickup scheduling), and listed on Shiprocket's official API docs (apidocs.shiprocket.in) plus MCP registries (Glama, mcpservers.org, LobeHub). (3) The claim does not overreach: it explicitly flags 'India's first' as company-asserted and unverified, which matches reality — the only sources for the superlative are the press release and PTI rewrite. (4) Timing arithmetic holds: May 2025 launch is ~13 months before mid-2026. Minor caveat: the MCP server is a thin open-source wrapper around Shiprocket's existing API, so 'AI infrastructure' should be read modestly, but the claim's actual assertion (a shipped product existed) is demonstrably true.

### [1] CEO Saahil Goel personally and publicly framed AI-agent-driven autonomous operations as Shiprocket's strategic direction in May 2025, stating the company is building a 'new interface for eCommerce' where AI executes business decisions — a signal that the agentic-AI push is CEO-sponsored strategy rather than a side experiment.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://cxotoday.com/press-release/shiprocket-launches-indias-first-ai-integrated-mcp-server-for-ecommerce/ (primary)
Quote: "Saahil Goel, MD & CEO of Shiprocket, said: "At Shiprocket, we're building not just for scale, but for the future. Our MCP Server launch marks a transformative shift from manual workflows to autonomous operations powered by AI... This is more than just an integration, it's a new interface for eCommerce. We're enabling a world where AI doesn't just support business decisions, it executes them.""
Verifier evidence (high): Quote verified verbatim and dated: IndianWeb2 (published May 16, 2025) carries the identical Saahil Goel (MD & CEO) quote — "Our MCP Server launch marks a transformative shift from manual workflows to autonomous operations powered by AI... it's a new interface for eCommerce. We're enabling a world where AI doesn't just support business decisions, it executes them" — matching the cxotoday press release (cxotoday returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch, but the same release was independently carried by YourStory at /2025/05/, IndianWeb2, SMEStreet, Maritime Gateway, and BW Retail World, confirming date and attribution). Every factual element of the claim (CEO personally, publicly, May 2025, 'new interface for eCommerce', AI executing decisions) is supported. The inferential clause ('a signal that the agentic-AI push is CEO-sponsored strategy rather than a side experiment') is hedged and independently corroborated by later reporting: BusinessToday (Nov 20, 2025) 'Inside Shiprocket's AI awakening' describes AI/agent pods hiring and agents in production; Storyboard18 reports Shiprocket refreshing its Rs 2,342 crore IPO filing with an AI-led growth focus; Tribune India (Feb 2026) has Goel publicly stating AI will drive e-commerce access for 60M MSMEs. A search for contradicting evidence (deprioritization, shutdown, pivot of the agentic strategy) found none. Caveat: the source is a press release, so marketing language ('India's first', 'transformative') should not be read as proof of execution quality — but the claim only asserts what the CEO publicly said and how he framed it, for which the launch announcement is the appropriate primary source.

### [2] The MCP server exposes concrete, falsifiable seller-facing capabilities to AI agents — rate checks, order tracking, shipment creation/cancellation, courier assignment, pickup scheduling — via natural-language instruction, replacing dashboards/APIs. This is the same agentic-commerce-for-sellers domain the candidate's prospective AI team would build on.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://cxotoday.com/press-release/shiprocket-launches-indias-first-ai-integrated-mcp-server-for-ecommerce/ (primary)
Quote: "Once integrated, AI agents can estimate delivery timelines, check courier rates, track orders, create or cancel shipments, assign couriers based on smart rules, list pickup addresses, or schedule pickups—all with a single line of instruction."
Verifier evidence (high): Claim survives adversarial checks. (1) The capability list is not just PR copy — it is independently verified against Shiprocket's official open-source MCP server repo (github.com/bfrs/shiprocket-mcp, owned by GitHub org 'bfrs' = Bigfoot Retail Solutions, Shiprocket's parent entity; committer 'Ajit Verma (BFRS01514)' / ajit-shiprocket). README tool list maps one-to-one to the claim: shipping_rate_calculator (rate checks), order_track (tracking), order_create/order_cancel (shipment creation/cancellation), order_ship 'based on the configured rules' (courier assignment via smart rules), order_pickup_schedule + list_pickup_addresses (pickup scheduling), estimated_date_of_delivery. (2) Launch (May 17, 2025) corroborated by multiple outlets beyond the PR wire, including independent editorial coverage at YourStory (yourstory.com/2025/05/shiprocket-unveils-indias-first-ai-integrated-mcp-server), SMEStreet, IndianWeb2, Maritime Gateway. (3) Not outdated/abandoned: repo's latest commit is 2025-11-17 (merged PR #10), ~7 months before today (June 2026); no evidence of discontinuation. (4) The capabilities are literally 'falsifiable' as claimed — the server is public, installable (Node 20-22, Claude Desktop/Cursor config), and connects to a real seller account. (5) Domain match to the candidate's prospective team (agentic commerce / AI agents for sellers) is a sound inference: this is exactly seller-facing agentic tooling. One qualification, not rising to refutation: 'replacing dashboards/APIs' echoes the press release's marketing line ('eliminating the need for traditional dashboards or APIs'); in reality the MCP server wraps Shiprocket's existing APIs and requires seller credentials, so 'replacing' should be read as company positioning rather than verified adoption behavior. The synthesizer should keep the capability list as verified fact and attribute the 'replaces dashboards' framing to Shiprocket.

### [3] In late August 2023, Omuni — the omnichannel retail platform owned by Shiprocket — laid off approximately 35% of its workforce (around 60-70 employees), with cuts hitting tech, product, sales, and talent acquisition teams.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://www.latestly.com/technology/layoffs-shiprocket-owned-omuni-lays-off-35-of-workforce-job-cuts-imapct-employees-in-tech-and-sales-teams-5377743.html (secondary)
Quote: "Shiprocket-Owned Omuni Lays Off 35% of Workforce, Cuts Hit Tech and Sales Teams ... affecting around 60-70 employees [across] tech, product, sales, and talent acquisition teams"
Verifier evidence (high): Claim verified against primary source: Inc42 exclusive (Aug 30, 2023) reported Omuni laid off ~60-70 employees ("nearly 35% of its workforce") from tech, product, sales, and talent acquisition teams, with two months' severance, and CEO Mukul Bafna and CTO Sumeet Chandhok exiting. Shiprocket officially confirmed on record: "As we explore synergies with acquisitions, including Omuni, it often results in the consolidation of the workforce at an organisation-wide level." Independently corroborated by IANS wire republications (investing.com, prokerala, BW People, dtnext) and LatestLY. One minor caveat: the layoffs occurred in the SECOND week of August 2023 per Inc42; "late August 2023" in the claim is when the news was reported (Aug 30-31), not when the cuts happened. All substantive figures and team details are accurate and uncontested by any source.

### [4] Shiprocket officially attributed the Omuni layoffs to post-acquisition workforce consolidation, indicating a pattern where acquired teams are downsized as they are integrated ('synergies').
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://www.latestly.com/technology/layoffs-shiprocket-owned-omuni-lays-off-35-of-workforce-job-cuts-imapct-employees-in-tech-and-sales-teams-5377743.html (secondary)
Quote: "As we explore synergies with acquisitions, including Omuni, it often results in the consolidation of the workforce."
Verifier evidence (high): Quote verified verbatim. The Latestly article (Aug 31, 2023) carries an official Shiprocket spokesperson statement: "As we explore synergies with acquisitions, including Omuni, it often results in the consolidation of the workforce at an organisation-wide level and we have integrated some teams across various group companies." The identical statement appears in the original Inc42 exclusive (https://inc42.com/buzz/exclusive-shiprocket-owned-omuni-fires-nearly-35-workforce-ceo-cto-to-exit/) and IANS wire syndications (in.investing.com, dtnext.in, bwpeople.in), confirming ~60-70 employees (~35%) cut across tech/product/sales/TA, with Omuni CEO Mukul Bafna and CTO Sumeet Chandhok exiting and 2 months severance paid. The claim's first half (official attribution to post-acquisition consolidation) is directly supported; the "pattern" inference is supported by the company's own generalizing wording — "acquisitions" plural, "including Omuni," and "it often results" — so it is Shiprocket itself describing consolidation as a recurring outcome of acquisitions, not an analyst overreach. No contradicting source found. Latestly is secondary, but the underlying Inc42/IANS reporting is credible and the claim is not extraordinary. Event date (Aug 2023) is appropriate for a historical acquisition-risk claim.

### [5] Shiprocket's consolidated net loss narrowed roughly 87.5% to INR 74.5 Cr in FY25 (year ended March 2025), down from INR 595.2 Cr in FY24.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://inc42.com/buzz/ipo-bound-shiprockets-fy25-loss-narrows-88-to-inr-74-5-cr/ (secondary)
Quote: "consolidated net loss decline 87.5% to INR 74.5 Cr in the year ended March 2025 from INR 595.2 Cr in FY24"
Verifier evidence (high): Claim verified against multiple independent sources. (1) Inc42 (30 Oct 2025) states verbatim: "consolidated net loss decline 87.5% to INR 74.5 Cr in the year ended March 2025 from INR 595.2 Cr in FY24" — the claim matches the quote exactly with no overreach. (2) Independent corroboration: Entrackr (30 Oct 2025), citing annual financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies, reports FY25 loss of Rs 74.4 Cr vs Rs 595 Cr in FY24 (0.1 Cr rounding difference only). (3) The FY24 baseline of Rs 595 Cr is separately confirmed by Oct-2024 reporting in Business Standard ("Shiprocket loss widens to Rs 595 cr in FY24 on restructuring costs") and IANS. (4) Arithmetic checks: (595.2-74.5)/595.2 = 87.5%. (5) Data is from statutory RoC filings, not a press release; FY25 is the latest completed fiscal year as of June 2026, so not outdated. Caveat for the final report (not a refutation): the FY24 loss included ~Rs 244 Cr one-time exceptional/restructuring items and ~Rs 190 Cr ESOP expense, so the 87.5% narrowing partly reflects non-recurrence of one-offs; Inc42 also notes FY25 would have been profitable but for Rs 91 Cr ESOP costs, and Entrackr notes FY25 cash EBITDA turned positive (Rs 7 Cr).

### [6] Shiprocket's operating revenue grew 24% year-over-year to INR 1,632 Cr in FY25 from INR 1,316 Cr in FY24, with core logistics contributing INR 1,306 Cr and emerging segments (cross-border, marketing, payments, omnichannel) contributing INR 326 Cr.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://inc42.com/buzz/ipo-bound-shiprockets-fy25-loss-narrows-88-to-inr-74-5-cr/ (secondary)
Quote: "revenue grew 24% YoY to INR 1,632 Cr in FY25 from INR 1,316 Cr in the previous fiscal year"
Verifier evidence (high): Claim verified against the cited Inc42 article and three independent outlets. Inc42 states verbatim: "revenue grew 24% YoY to INR 1,632 Cr in FY25 from INR 1,316 Cr in the previous fiscal year," with core logistics/tech business at "INR 1,306 Cr" and "INR 326 Cr from emerging segments such as cross-border, marketing, payments, and omnichannel" (arithmetic consistent: 1,306+326=1,632). Independently corroborated by Entrackr (Oct 30, 2025: Rs 1,632 Cr revenue, core up 20% YoY to Rs 1,306 Cr at ~80% of revenue, emerging up 41% YoY to Rs 326 Cr), YourStory, and BW Disrupt — all reporting from FY25 annual-report/RoC filings. The claim correctly says "operating revenue" (Inc42 separately reports total income incl. other income at INR 1,675 Cr). Figures are the latest full-year results available as of June 2026 (FY ended March 2025, reported Oct 2025), so not outdated. Minor caveat: numbers originate in pre-IPO company filings, but multi-outlet filing-based reporting is adequate source quality for a routine revenue claim.

### [7] Shiprocket turned cash EBITDA positive in FY25 at INR 7 Cr, compared with a cash burn of INR 128 Cr in FY24 — a key signal of improving company health and runway stability.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://inc42.com/buzz/ipo-bound-shiprockets-fy25-loss-narrows-88-to-inr-74-5-cr/ (secondary)
Quote: "turned cash EBITDA positive in FY25 at INR 7 Cr as against a burn of INR 128 Cr in the previous year"
Verifier evidence (high): Claim is a near-verbatim restatement of the Inc42 quote and is independently corroborated. Entrackr (30 Oct 2025) reports identical figures — "turned EBITDA cash positive at Rs 7 crore, compared to a burn of Rs 128 crore in FY24" — sourced from annual financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), i.e., primary filings, not merely the company press statement. Outlook Business ("Shiprocket Posts 1st Full-Year Positive Cash EBITDA"), YourStory, and BW Disrupt corroborate. Surrounding audited facts are consistent: net loss narrowed 87.5% to INR 74.5 Cr (from INR 595.2 Cr), revenue up 24% to INR 1,632 Cr, spend-per-rupee improved from Rs 1.30 to Rs 1.07. No contradicting source found. Caveats (not refuting): "cash EBITDA" is a non-GAAP, company-defined metric originating in Shiprocket's pre-IPO disclosure, and the company still posted a INR 74.5 Cr net loss — the "runway stability" gloss is interpretive but consistent with the data. FY25 (ended March 2025) remains the latest full-year audited data as of June 2026, so the claim is current.

### [8] Shiprocket filed its DRHP with SEBI via the confidential pre-filing route (in May 2025) for an IPO targeting roughly INR 2,000-2,500 Cr, including a fresh issue of INR 1,000-1,200 Cr — meaning the IPO was formally in motion as of late 2025.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://inc42.com/buzz/ipo-bound-shiprockets-fy25-loss-narrows-88-to-inr-74-5-cr/ (secondary)
Quote: "filed its DRHP with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) via the confidential pre-filing route ... around INR 2,000 Cr to INR 2,500 Cr ... a fresh issue of shares worth INR 1,000 Cr to INR 1,200 Cr"
Verifier evidence (high): Claim is fully supported by the cited Inc42 article (Oct 30, 2025), which states verbatim that "In May, the Delhi NCR-based company filed its DRHP with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) via the confidential pre-filing route to raise around INR 2,000 Cr to INR 2,500 Cr through its IPO. The issue will include a fresh issue of shares worth INR 1,000 Cr to INR 1,200 Cr." Crucially, primary-source corroboration exists: SEBI's own website lists Shiprocket Limited's Updated DRHP (UDRHP) filed December 12-15, 2025 (https://www.sebi.gov.in/filings/public-issues/dec-2025/shiprocket-limited-udrhp_98357.html), confirming the IPO was formally in motion as of late 2025. The UDRHP figures — ₹2,342.3 Cr total issue with ₹1,100 Cr fresh issue (per Medianama, Angel One) — fall within the claimed ranges of ~INR 2,000-2,500 Cr and INR 1,000-1,200 Cr respectively. SEBI reportedly issued its observation letter approving the IPO on Oct 31, 2025 (Kotak Securities). Multiple independent outlets (Inc42, Groww, Upstox, Kotak, Medianama, Angel One) corroborate the May 2025 confidential pre-filing. No contradicting evidence found; the only minor variance is one estimate of fresh capital at ₹1,200-1,400 Cr (Kotak), but the actual UDRHP figure of ₹1,100 Cr validates the claim's 1,000-1,200 Cr range. Claim is current as of the research date (June 2026) for its stated scope ("as of late 2025"); expected listing is H1 FY27.

### [9] Shiprocket filed an updated DRHP (December 2025) for an INR 2,342.3 Cr IPO, comprising a fresh issue of up to INR 1,100 Cr and an offer-for-sale of up to INR 1,242.3 Cr, after filing a confidential DRHP in May 2025 and receiving SEBI approval in November 2025 — meaning the IPO was formally in motion heading into 2026.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://inc42.com/buzz/eternal-backed-shiprocket-files-updated-drhp-for-inr-2342-cr-ipo/ (secondary)
Quote: "The company's proposed public listing will comprise a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to INR 1,100 Cr and an OFS component of up to INR 1,242.3 Cr. ... Shiprocket filed its confidential DRHP with SEBI in May and received the market regulator's nod to float the IPO in November."
Verifier evidence (high): All material elements independently corroborated, including by a primary source. (1) SEBI's own filings page lists "Shiprocket Limited - UDRHP" under December 2025 public-issue filings (sebi.gov.in/filings/public-issues/dec-2025/shiprocket-limited-udrhp_98357.html) — primary confirmation the updated DRHP was filed Dec 2025 (Dec 12, 2025 per aggregators). (2) IPO size/structure confirmed by multiple independent outlets: total INR 2,342.35 Cr = fresh issue up to INR 1,100 Cr + OFS up to INR 1,242.35 Cr (Entrackr, Dec 13, 2025: "Shiprocket files updated DRHP to raise Rs 1,100 Cr via fresh issue"; Outlook Money; Zerodha/Chittorgarh IPO pages). (3) Confidential DRHP pre-filed May 2025 confirmed by Entrackr (Nov 3, 2025) and Groww. (4) One nuance: SEBI's observation letter was formally dated October 31, 2025 (per SEBI processing status, reported by Entrackr Nov 3, 2025), so "SEBI approval in November 2025" is off by one day on the letter date — the approval became public/reported in early November, which is how Inc42 and others framed it. This is immaterial to the claim's substance. (5) "IPO formally in motion heading into 2026" holds as of June 2026: brokerage IPO trackers (Zerodha, INDmoney, ICICI Direct) show the UDRHP filed, SEBI approval in hand, and listing date still TBA — no evidence of withdrawal or shelving. Inc42 is a reputable Indian startup-news outlet and its figures match the SEBI primary filing, so source quality matches claim strength.

### [10] Shiprocket's FY25 operating revenue grew 24% YoY to INR 1,632 Cr (from INR 1,316 Cr in FY24), while net loss narrowed 88% to INR 74.5 Cr (from INR 595.2 Cr) — i.e., the company was still loss-making in FY25 but rapidly approaching breakeven.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://inc42.com/buzz/eternal-backed-shiprocket-files-updated-drhp-for-inr-2342-cr-ipo/ (secondary)
Quote: "Its operating revenue grew 24% YoY to INR 1,632 Cr from INR 1,316 Cr in FY24 ... net loss by 88% to INR 74.5 Cr in FY25 from INR 595.2 Cr in the previous year."
Verifier evidence (high): Claim is verbatim-supported by the cited Inc42 DRHP article (Dec 13, 2025) and independently corroborated by Entrackr (Oct 30, 2025), which sourced the same figures from Shiprocket's annual financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies: FY25 operating revenue Rs 1,632 Cr vs Rs 1,316 Cr in FY24 (exactly 24.0% YoY), net loss Rs 74.4-74.5 Cr vs Rs 595-595.2 Cr (87.5% reduction; '88%' is rounding). YourStory and a second Inc42 piece report identical numbers. The 'approaching breakeven' interpretation is supported by Shiprocket turning EBITDA positive (~Rs 7 Cr) in FY25 vs a Rs 128 Cr burn in FY24. Underlying data is from regulatory filings (RoC + SEBI DRHP), i.e., primary-quality; FY25 is the latest full-year audited result available as of June 2026, so the claim is current. No contradicting source found.

### [11] Shiprocket's revenue grew 24% year-on-year to Rs 1,632 crore in FY25 (financial year ended March 2025).
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://www.bwdisrupt.com/article/ipo-bound-shiprocket-s-revenue-rises-24-fy25-net-loss-narrows-577557 (secondary)
Quote: "The company’s revenue rose 24 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,632 crore, supported by steady expansion in its shipping business and a rapid rise in new service lines, as per media reports."
Verifier evidence (high): Claim is well-supported and traces to primary filings. Entrackr (Oct 30, 2025) reports FY25 operating revenue of Rs 1,632 crore, up 24% from Rs 1,316 crore in FY24, citing "the annual financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC)" and a confirming quote from Shiprocket CFO Tanmay Kumar (https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/shiprocket-posts-rs-1632-cr-revenue-in-fy25-narrows-losses-to-rs-74-cr-10607230). Arithmetic verifies exactly: 1632/1316 = 1.240 (24% YoY). Independently corroborated by Angel One, Whalesbook, startupnews.fyi, and the cited BW Disrupt piece. The same reporting also discloses a Rs 74 crore FY25 net loss, so this is balanced financial reporting, not promotional spin. Only minor nuance: Rs 1,632 Cr is operating revenue (revenue from operations), which matches the claim's standard phrasing. Claim is current — FY25 ended March 2025, filings made Oct 2025, no later restatement found as of June 2026.

### [12] Shiprocket turned adjusted-EBITDA positive in FY25, reporting Rs 7 crore adjusted EBITDA versus an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 128 crore in FY24.
Vote: 3-0 · Source: https://www.bwdisrupt.com/article/ipo-bound-shiprocket-s-revenue-rises-24-fy25-net-loss-narrows-577557 (secondary)
Quote: "Logistics-tech unicorn Shiprocket reported a significant improvement in profitability for the financial year ended March 2025, recording a positive adjusted Ebitda of Rs 7 crore compared to a loss of Rs 128 crore in FY24."
Verifier evidence (high): Claim is a faithful restatement of the cited quote and is independently corroborated by at least three outlets reporting from Shiprocket's RoC filings and DRHP: Entrackr (30 Oct 2025) — "turned EBITDA cash positive at Rs 7 crore, compared to a Rs 128 crore burn in FY24," per "annual financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC)"; Outlook Business (30 Oct 2025) — "positive adjusted EBITDA of ₹7 crore" vs "cash burn of ₹128 crore in FY24"; figures also consistent with updated DRHP coverage (Inc42, Angel One). No contradicting source found. Claim correctly does NOT overreach to net profitability (FY25 net loss was still Rs 74.4 Cr, down 88% from Rs 595 Cr). Minor caveat: outlets use "adjusted EBITDA" and "cash EBITDA" interchangeably for the same Rs 7 Cr non-GAAP, company-defined metric, framed favorably ahead of the IPO — but the claim transparently labels the metric, so this is a framing nuance, not an error.

### [13] Shiprocket's net loss narrowed sharply to Rs 74 crore in FY25 from Rs 595 crore in FY24, with the FY24 figure inflated by one-time restructuring and accounting expenses; cash profit from the core business doubled to Rs 157 crore.
Vote: 2-0 · Source: https://www.bwdisrupt.com/article/ipo-bound-shiprocket-s-revenue-rises-24-fy25-net-loss-narrows-577557 (secondary)
Quote: "Improved Ebitda performance also led to a reduction in the company’s net loss to Rs 74 crore, compared to Rs 595 crore in FY24, which had included one-time restructuring and accounting expenses."
Verifier evidence (high): Claim survives adversarial checks; each element is independently corroborated by outlets citing Shiprocket's annual financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). (1) Net loss figures: Entrackr (Oct 30, 2025) reports FY25 net loss Rs 74.4 Cr vs Rs 595 Cr in FY24; Inc42 reports "consolidated net loss declined 87.5% to INR 74.5 Cr in the year ended March 2025 from INR 595.2 Cr in FY24" — matching the claim's Rs 74 Cr / Rs 595 Cr. (2) FY24 inflation by one-time items: Entrackr's RoC-based breakdown shows FY24's Rs 595 Cr loss included Rs 240 Cr in exceptional items plus Rs 190 Cr ESOP expenses (~Rs 430 Cr combined), substantiating the "one-time restructuring and accounting expenses" framing rather than it being mere company spin. (3) Cash profit: Entrackr reports core business (domestic shipping + merchant-tech) cash EBITDA of Rs 157 Cr in FY25, a "2.2X YoY improvement" — so "doubled to Rs 157 crore" is supported and if anything slightly understated. Timeliness: FY25 (ended March 2025) is the latest full-year filing available as of June 2026 (FY26 results not yet filed), so the claim is current. Caveats (not refuting): "cash profit" is the company's non-standard "cash EBITDA" metric, and the one-time-expense framing originates partly from company messaging echoed by media; company-wide (not core-only) cash EBITDA was only Rs 7 Cr positive, and the company remains net-loss-making. These nuances qualify but do not contradict the claim as stated.


## Refuted claims (for transparency)
- "Shiprocket filed an updated DRHP with SEBI in December 2025 (after a confidential pre-filing in May 2025 and regulatory approval in November 2025) for an IPO of INR 2,342.3 Cr, comprising a fresh issue of up to INR 1,100 Cr and an offer-for-sale of up to INR 1,242.3 Cr — confirming the IPO was actively in motion heading into 2026." (https://inc42.com/buzz/shiprocket-drhp-a-look-at-shareholding-pattern-key-executives/, vote 0-0)

- vercel-plugin:ai-elements: AI Elements component library guidance — pre-built React components for AI interfaces built on shadcn/ui. Use when building chat UIs, message displays, tool call rendering, streaming responses, reasoning panels, or any AI-native interface with the AI SDK.
- vercel-plugin:ai-gateway: Vercel AI Gateway expert guidance. Use when configuring model routing, provider failover, cost tracking, or managing multiple AI providers through a unified API.
- vercel-plugin:ai-sdk: Vercel AI SDK expert guidance. Use when building AI-powered features — chat interfaces, text generation, structured output, tool calling, agents, MCP integration, streaming, embeddings, reranking, image generation, or working with any LLM provider.
- vercel-plugin:auth: Authentication integration guidance — Clerk (native Vercel Marketplace), Descope, and Auth0 setup for Next.js applications. Covers middleware auth patterns, sign-in/sign-up flows, and Marketplace provisioning. Use when implementing user authentication.
- vercel-plugin:bootstrap: Project bootstrapping orchestrator for repos that depend on Vercel-linked resources (databases, auth, and managed integrations). Use when setting up or repairing a repository so linking, environment provisioning, env pulls, and first-run db/dev commands happen in the correct safe order.
- vercel-plugin:chat-sdk: Vercel Chat SDK expert guidance. Use when building multi-platform chat bots — Slack, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, GitHub, Linear — with a single codebase. Covers the Chat class, adapters, threads, messages, cards, modals, streaming, state management, and webhook setup.
- vercel-plugin:cron-jobs: Vercel Cron Jobs configuration and best practices. Use when adding, editing, or debugging scheduled tasks in vercel.json.
- vercel-plugin:deployments-cicd: Vercel deployment and CI/CD expert guidance. Use when deploying, promoting, rolling back, inspecting deployments, building with --prebuilt, or configuring CI workflow files for Vercel.
- vercel-plugin:env-vars: Vercel environment variable expert guidance. Use when working with .env files, vercel env commands, OIDC tokens, or managing environment-specific configuration.
- vercel-plugin:investigation-mode: Orchestrated debugging coordinator. Triggers on frustration signals (stuck, hung, broken, waiting) and systematically triages: runtime logs → workflow status → browser verify → deploy/env. Reports findings at every step.
- vercel-plugin:json-render: AI chat response rendering guidance — handling UIMessage parts, tool call displays, streaming states, and structured data presentation. Use when building custom chat UIs, rendering tool results, or troubleshooting AI response display issues.
- vercel-plugin:knowledge-update: Corrects outdated LLM knowledge about the Vercel platform and introduces new products. Injected at session start.
- vercel-plugin:marketplace: Vercel Marketplace expert guidance — discovering, installing, and building integrations, auto-provisioned environment variables, unified billing, and the vercel integration CLI. Use when consuming third-party services, building custom integrations, or managing marketplace resources on Vercel.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
